blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: formar el superlativo con the -est o the most
decir que dos cosas son iguales con as ... as
describir movimientos con into, out of, across, through y otras preposiciones

blocks.text:
London is bigger than Amsterdam. — Londres es más grande que Ámsterdam.
This is the most beautiful beach in Spain. — Esta es la playa más bonita de España.
He's the best player in the team. — Es el mejor jugador del equipo.

blocks.title: más grande = bigger; de Europa = in Europe
bullets: más grande que = bigger than, no more big. Las palabras cortas llevan -er; solo las largas llevan more. Y que es than, no that ni then.
Después de un superlativo con un lugar o un grupo: in, no of. la montaña más alta de Europa = the highest mountain in Europe.
Nada de formas dobles: more bigger y most cheapest son incorrectos.

head: Inglés
Español
rows: Tom is as tall as his father.
Tom es tan alto como su padre.
This film isn't as good as the book.
Esta película no es tan buena como el libro.
My car is the same as yours.
Mi coche es igual que el tuyo.
Ella es distinta de su hermana.

head: Preposición
Ejemplo
Español
rows: He came out of the house.
We walked up the hill and down again.
Subimos la colina y volvimos a bajar.
The train goes through a tunnel.
El tren pasa por un túnel.
Paseamos a lo largo del río.
Pasa por delante de la iglesia.
The plane flew over the city.

blocks.title: El verbo dice cómo, la preposición dice adónde
blocks.text: El español pone la dirección en el verbo: entrar, salir, subir, bajar, cruzar. El inglés la pone en la preposición, y el verbo dice cómo te mueves: entró corriendo en la tienda = she ran into the shop, cruzamos la calle andando = we walked across the street, subió la montaña = he climbed up the mountain.

blocks.title: go to, pero arrive in / at
blocks.text: Movimiento hacia un lugar: go to school, come to the party. Pero llegar es arrive in (ciudad, país) o arrive at (edificio, estación): We arrived in London at six. We arrived at the hotel. Nunca arrive to, aunque en español digas llegar a. Y go home sin to.

rows: She is more tall than me.
Un lugar después de un superlativo: in.
He is as tall like his brother.
He is as tall as his brother.
We arrived to Madrid at nine.
We arrived in Madrid at nine.

blocks.text: Completa con la forma o la preposición correcta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: A car is ______ than a bike.
items.full: A car is faster than a bike.

items.q: This hotel is ______ than the other one.
items.full: This hotel is more expensive than the other one.

items.q: It was the ______ day of my life.
items.full: It was the best day of my life.

items.q: My exam was ______ than I expected.
items.full: My exam was worse than I expected.

items.q: He's the ______ student in the class.
items.full: He's the cleverest student in the class.

items.q: My bag isn't ______ heavy as yours.
items.full: My bag isn't as heavy as yours.

items.q: She ran ______ the shop to buy milk.
items.full: She ran into the shop to buy milk.

items.q: Walk ______ the bridge and turn left.
items.full: Walk across the bridge and turn left.

items.q: We arrived ______ the station at ten.
items.full: We arrived at the station at ten.

items.q: The train went ______ a long tunnel.
items.full: The train went through a long tunnel.

items.q: It's the ______ beautiful city in Italy.
items.full: It's the most beautiful city in Italy.

items.q: Londres es más grande que Ámsterdam.
Él es tan alto como su padre.
items.a: He is as tall as his father.

items.q: Es la montaña más alta de Europa.
items.a: It is the highest mountain in Europe.
